Trellops Feature Tour

A complete step-by-step guide from first login to live dashboards, maps, and AI summaries. Follow the steps in order or jump to any section using the sidebar.

Step 1 · Getting Started

Welcome & Login

Trellops works entirely with your existing Trello account. No new account is needed — just authorise access and you are ready to go.

Open Trellops

Visit trellops.xyz in any modern browser. You will land on the home page.

Click "Try Trellops Now"

Hit the main call-to-action button on the home page, or the Login with Trello button in the footer.

Authorise with Trello

A Trello popup will appear. Log in with your Atlassian account and click Allow. Trellops requests Read-only access by default — it cannot modify your boards without explicit additional permission.

✓
Trellops follows a Local First principle. Your API token is stored only in your browser and is never sent to our servers.
Next: Connect Your Board →

Step 2 · Getting Started

Connect Your Board

After logging in, Trellops will load and present you with a board selection screen. This is the first decision that shapes your entire dashboard.

Pick a Trello Board

All boards you have access to will be listed. Click the one you want to build a dashboard for. You can switch boards at any time from the Settings screen.

Wait for data to load

Trellops will fetch your board's lists, cards, and labels in the background. A spinner will be visible while data loads — this usually takes just a second or two.

← Back Next: Create Blocks →

Step 3 · Dashboard Setup

Create Blocks

Blocks are the building blocks of your dashboard. They let you group related Trello lists together visually — for example, grouping "To Do", "In Progress", and "Waiting" under a single "Active Work" section.

Open Settings

Click the Settings button in the footer of your dashboard. The settings panel will open on the Dashboard tab by default.

Create your first Block

In the Dashboard tab, click "+ Add Block" (or equivalent add button). Type a meaningful name for the group, such as Backlog, Active, or Done.

Add more Blocks as needed

Repeat the process for each logical group you want to show. Most boards work well with 2–4 blocks. You can always add, rename, or delete blocks later.

Show or hide a Block

Each block has a visibility toggle. Hide a block (e.g. "Archive") to keep your main dashboard clean without deleting the configuration.

← Back Next: Assign & Order Tiles →

Step 4 · Dashboard Setup

Assign & Order Tiles

Each Trello list becomes a coloured "tile" on your dashboard. Tiles need to be assigned to a Block before they will appear in your dashboard view.

Find the Unassigned list

Below your blocks in the Settings panel, you will see all the lists from your Trello board under "Unassigned Lists". These are lists that have not been placed into a block yet.

Drag tiles into Blocks

Use the drag-and-drop interface to drag list tiles from the Unassigned area into any block you created. Tiles snap into position as you move them.

Reorder tiles within a Block

Within a block, drag tiles up or down to set the display order. The most important or highest-priority list is typically placed first.

Move tiles between Blocks

Simply drag a tile out of one block and drop it into another. You can also send tiles back to the Unassigned list to hide them from the dashboard.

← Back Next: Customise Tiles →

Step 5 · Dashboard Setup

Customise Tiles

Each tile can be individually configured to give it a distinct identity, correct counts, and visual cues for your team.

Set a tile colour

Click a tile in the Settings panel to open its configuration. Use the colour picker to assign a specific colour — Red for urgent, Green for completed, and so on. If you don't pick one, a random colour is assigned automatically.

Ignore the first card (Description Cards)

If the first card in a Trello list is a header or instruction card (not a real work item), enable "Don't count the first card". This keeps your totals accurate.

Display the first card as a description

Enable "Display as description" to show the text of the first card directly on the tile on your main dashboard — useful as a live status indicator or summary for your team.

ℹ
Click any live tile on your main dashboard to open a detailed card list for that list — showing card names, due dates, members, labels, and comments.
← Back Next: Customise Blocks →

Step 6 · Dashboard Setup

Customise Blocks

Beyond grouping tiles, blocks themselves can be configured with names and icons for the Map View, and collapsed to clean up your dashboard.

Rename a Block

Click the block name in the settings panel to edit it. Choose a name that communicates the phase or status of work — e.g. "In Progress" or "Awaiting Client".

Assign a Map Icon

In the Map Settings tab, you can assign a unique icon to each block. Cards from that block will appear on the map with your chosen icon — very useful for distinguishing job types (e.g. 🔧 Maintenance vs 🏗️ New Build).

Collapse a Block on the dashboard

On your live dashboard, click the eye icon next to any block header to collapse it. The block is hidden temporarily — no data is lost, and you can expand it again at any time.

← Back Next: General & Display →

Step 7 · Other Settings

General & Display Options

Head to the Other tab inside Settings for general display and behaviour preferences.

Theme: Light or Dark Mode

Toggle between Light, Dark, or System (follows your OS preference) using the theme button in any view's header. The setting persists across sessions.

Digital Clock

Enable the large digital clock display in the top-left corner — ideal for wall-mounted screens and operations centres. Configure it per board in the Other Settings tab.

Prevent Screen Off

Use the monitor icon in the dashboard header to prevent your screen from sleeping — perfect for always-on wall displays.

Auto-refresh Interval

Trellops refreshes data from Trello automatically. The refresh countdown is shown in the dashboard footer. You can manually trigger a refresh at any time by clicking the refresh button.

Slideshow Mode

Enable Slideshow to automatically cycle between your Dashboard and Map views at a configurable interval. Great for NOC displays. Start it using the arrow buttons in the footer.

Export, Import, and Clear Config

Under Other Settings, you can export your entire configuration to a JSON file, import a colleague's config, or clear local storage to start fresh. Note: Clear is irreversible.

← Back Next: Naming & Terminology →

Step 8 · Other Settings

Naming & Terminology

Different teams call things by different names. Trellops lets you replace generic Trello vocabulary with terms that match your organisation's language.

Open Naming Config

In Settings → Other Settings, scroll down to find the Naming Config section.

Set custom terms

Override any of the following defaults:

Board → e.g. Project
Card → e.g. Task or Job
List → e.g. Stage or Column
Label → e.g. Tag or Category

See changes apply instantly

Your custom terms will appear in the Dashboard header filters, Statistics view charts, and the AI Summary output — making the entire app feel native to your team.

← Back Next: Enable Statistics →

Step 9 · Statistics & AI

Enable & Explore Statistics

The Statistics view gives you powerful charts and time-based insights into your team's activity — no manual spreadsheets required.

Enable Statistics in Settings

In Settings → Other Settings, find the Statistics toggle and enable it. A Stats button will appear in your dashboard header.

Open the Statistics view

Click the Stats button in the dashboard header, or navigate directly to /stats in the URL. The page will load and begin analysing your board data.

Choose a time period

Use the period filter dropdown at the top (e.g. This Week, Last Month, Custom Range) to scope the data shown in all charts.

Filter by Labels

Use the Labels filter (or your custom term) in the header to narrow charts down to specific categories of work.

Read the charts

Charts include: cards created over time, cards per list, due-date completion, and a label/tag breakdown donut chart — all updating live as you change filters.

← Back Next: AI Summary →

Step 10 · Statistics & AI

AI Summary Beta

The AI Summary feature reads your board data for the selected period and produces a plain-English briefing — who did what, what is overdue, what is progressing well.

Generate a summary

In the Statistics view, find the AI Summary card at the top of the page. Click "Generate Summary". The AI will analyse the cards in scope and stream a response in seconds.

Add a Custom AI Prompt

For more tailored output, head to Settings → Other Settings → Custom AI Prompt. Enter an instruction such as:

"Write this as a concise morning briefing for a field operations manager."
"Focus only on overdue cards and flag any card assigned to multiple members."

Improve your prompt with AI

Once you have written a draft prompt, click "Improve with AI" next to the text area. The AI will rewrite and enhance your instruction for better results.

Understand what data is sent

Card names, descriptions, comments, members, and labels within the selected time window are sent securely to Google Cloud (Gemini) for processing. No data is retained by Google after the response. See our Privacy Policy for details.

⚠
The AI Summary is a Beta feature and powered by Google Gemini. Usage is subject to rate limits. If you see an error, wait a moment and try again — daily limits reset automatically.
← Back Next: Configure Map Settings →

Step 11 · Map View

Configure Map Settings

Before opening the Map View, configure how Trellops should plot your cards and what they should look like on the map.

Enable the Map View

In Settings → Map, enable the "Enable Map View" toggle. A Map button will then appear in your dashboard footer.

Set a Home Address (optional)

Enter your office or HQ address in the Home Address field. This will place a distinctive home marker on the map and be used as the default centre point when no cards are visible.

Assign Block Icons

In the Map Settings tab, click on each Block to assign it a custom icon (e.g. 🔧, 🚗, 📦). This icon will appear on map pins for cards within that block.

Configure Label Icon Overrides

You can also override the pin icon based on a Trello label applied to a card. For example, all cards with a "Urgent" label could display a 🔥 icon regardless of which block they belong to.

Enable Street View (optional)

Toggle "Show Street View" in the Map Settings to add a Google Street View link inside every map pin popup. Clicking it will open a Street View at the card's location in a new tab.

Enable Card Move (requires Write permission)

To allow cards to be moved between lists directly from the map, enable "Enable card move". You will be prompted to re-login with Write access to Trello. This is a separate, optional permission.

← Back Next: Your First Map View →

Step 12 · Map View

Your First Map View

With settings in place, you are ready to explore your cards geographically.

Open the Map View

Click the Map button in the dashboard footer. The map will load and begin geocoding addresses found in your card descriptions.

How cards are plotted

Trellops plots cards using two methods:

1. Coordinates: If a card has latitude/longitude stored in it (from a previous Trellops session or plugin), it plots instantly.
2. Address Geocoding: If no coordinates are found, Trellops reads the card description and uses Google Maps to find a location. This is cached after the first load.

Click a pin to see card details

Click any map marker to open a popup with the card name, assigned list, labels, and (if enabled) a Street View link.

Use "Fit Map" to see everything

Click the Fit Map button to automatically zoom the map to show all visible pins. If only one pin is visible, the map zooms to a comfortable street level rather than zooming in all the way.

Filter what you see

Use the map filter panel to show/hide cards by Block, Label, or list. Filters update the map in real time.

Move cards between lists (if Write enabled)

Open a card's popup on the map, then use the Move to list control to reassign the card to a different Trello list directly from the map interface.

✓
Geocoded locations are cached in your browser. The next time you open the map, all previously resolved addresses load instantly — no waiting.
